source: Collated from worker-1..5-trajectory.md and verify-round-1-trajectory.md in this directory
categories: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain

tools.name: CodeRabbit
tools.standout: Most complete workflow: chat, one-click fixes, Triage, learnings, CLI/IDE, security+dependency scans; 2M reviews/wk; valued $550M to $1.5B in 11 months; a review-bot RCE with write access was demonstrated on 1M repos.
tools.triage: PR summary, inline comments, Triage queue, one-click fixes.
tools.context: Diff + repo context; learns from accepted comments; no per-line provenance.
tools.pricing: Free public repos; Essentials $24/dev/mo annual ($30 mo); Team $48/$60; $0.25/reviewed file continued.
tools.stack: LLM over diff + repo context; multi-host.

tools.name: Greptile
tools.what: Codebase-aware LLM reviewer with full-codebase index.
tools.standout: Builds a complete graph of the codebase (files/functions/vars/imports/calls); parallel review agents; learns from comments; TREX agent writes and runs tests in a sandbox.
tools.triage: PR comments + summary; TREX test evidence.
tools.context: Full codebase graph + agentic multi-hop search.
tools.pricing: Free (1 dev, 50 credits); Pro $30/seat/mo incl 50 credits, $1/extra; TREX = 3 credits; Chat +$20/user.

tools.name: Macroscope
tools.standout: Language-specific codewalkers + AST/reference graph; Check Run Agents (named required checks, per-agent model routing, external tool calls); Fix It For Me CI autofix loop; Approvability.
tools.conflict: None; Check Runs can be required checks.
tools.triage: GitHub Checks + auto-fix PR; CI-failure read-and-retry loop.
tools.context: AST per file + reference graph; deterministic parsers.
tools.pricing: $0.05/KB reviewed (10KB min = $0.50 floor; ~$0.95 avg); $100 free; Agent included.
tools.stack: Language parsers + deterministic check runs; GitHub-only.

tools.name: Qodo Merge / PR-Agent
tools.standout: Open-source PR-Agent core; Rule System across devs and agents; Enterprise Gerrit/on-prem; repackaged from per-seat to pooled credits in 2026.
tools.pricing: Pooled credits $0.012/credit; $30 pack = 2,500 credits (~18 reviews); 14-day trial; free tier and per-seat dropped.
tools.stack: Context engine + rules; OSS core + enterprise.

tools.name: Codacy
tools.what: Deterministic governance reviewer that fails closed.
tools.standout: Deterministic gates that fail closed (only the rule/threshold tier reliably blocks a merge); Verity blocks on prompt-conformance (unique); MCP server; AI overlay on a rule engine.
tools.stack: Rule engine + gates + AI overlay; MCP server.

tools.name: Cursor Bugbot
tools.standout: Auto-runs on PR update or /review-bugbot; fail-on-unresolved org-gated; benchmarked 29/58% (Greptile study) and 42% (Macroscope study).
tools.triage: Cursor editor + PR review; fail-on-unresolved gate.

tools.name: Trunk
tools.standout: Predictive testing against a projected head so merged SHA equals tested SHA; parallel lanes; batching; anti-flake; CI-layer flaky detection/quarantine; priority merging; direct-merge-to-main.
tools.conflict: Queue ordering; no semantic conflict engine.
tools.pricing: Free <=5 committers/5M spans; Team <=50; Enterprise custom.

tools.name: Aviator
tools.what: Merge queue with monorepo routing and self-hosting.
tools.standout: Affected-targets routing via build graph (Bazel/NX/Pants/Turborepo/Gradle); ChangeSets cross-repo coordination; FlexReview; real self-hosting; MIT av CLI; SOC 2 Type II.

tools.name: Mergify
tools.what: GitHub merge queue with batching and bisect.
tools.standout: Batching + bisect-on-batch-failure; CI Insights; Test Insights (flaky quarantine); Merge Protections; YAML rules; 2k+ orgs merging 75k+ PRs/mo.

tools.name: Graphite
tools.what: Stacked-diff workflow + merge queue + AI review.
tools.standout: Stack-aware merge queue; gt CLI; AI review (ex-Diamond); PR inbox; dev metrics; MCP; Cursor Cloud Agents; adoption at Shopify/Vercel/Snowflake/Figma/X; $72M raised.
tools.pricing: Hobby free; Starter $20; Team $40; Enterprise custom.
tools.stack: Closed-source CLI + GitHub app + server queue.

tools.name: GitButler
tools.standout: Multiple virtual branches in one working tree; drag hunks between lanes; commit/push each independently; agents via but CLI; vendor benchmark: agents ~65% faster with 78% fewer VCS commands (self-run).
tools.concurrency: Several virtual branches in one worktree (parallel streams).

tools.name: Jujutsu (jj)
tools.what: DAG-first branchless VCS over Git storage.
tools.standout: No staging area or current branch; rewriting a commit auto-rebases all descendants; operation-log undo; Git-compatible; conflicts first-class.
tools.concurrency: Concurrent lanes as changes (no branch names).
tools.conflict: Automatic descendant rebase; conflicts are first-class objects.

tools.name: Sapling
tools.what: Meta-scale VCS with first-class commit stacks.
tools.standout: First-class commit stacks; smartlog; amend/undo anywhere; proven at Meta scale (10M+ files); Mercurial-derived.

tools.name: Gerrit
tools.what: Central review forge with server-side submit queue.
tools.standout: Change-Id gives a logical change a stable identity across patchsets; refs/for/ upload; topics; server-side submit queue; per-project ACLs plus per-file OWNERS path grants.
tools.triage: Patchset review with stable change identity.

tools.name: Devin (Cognition)
tools.what: Cloud autonomous agent with fleet/migration mode.
tools.standout: Fleet of agents to migrate all repos in parallel; Devin Review generator-verifier loop; DeepWiki; manager Devin spawns child Devins via internal MCP; doctrine: multi-agent works only when writes stay single-threaded.
tools.concurrency: Fleet + child Devins via MCP; deliberately single-threaded writes.
tools.pricing: Free to $20 Pro to $200 Max; Teams $80 min; Enterprise custom; ACU ~ 15 min work.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex (cloud)
tools.standout: Parallel cloud tasks; 90+ MCP plugins (claim); subagent delegation; OS-native sandbox; Code review; GPT-5.x-Codex.
tools.pricing: Bundled in ChatGPT ($0 entry) / API $1.75/$14 per M.

tools.name: Google Jules
tools.standout: Published concurrency 3/15/60 by tier; 15/100/300 tasks/day; REST API (alpha); GitHub App; approval-gated plans; async VM to PR.
tools.pricing: Free to AI Pro $19.99 to AI Ultra $99.99+.

tools.name: Factory (Droids + Missions)
tools.what: Enterprise agent platform with Missions orchestration.
tools.standout: Subagents, Missions, Droid Computers, Connectors, Skills, Hooks; 'Agent Readiness'; states 'coordination is hard. Agents conflict, duplicate work, and drift without structure'; parallelizes only where coordination overhead is low; validation workers; git as source of truth.
tools.concurrency: Missions parallelize only low-coordination work; serialization by default.
tools.conflict: Serialization + targeted parallelism instead of conflict-aware merge.
tools.triage: Milestone/feature review; git as source of truth.

tools.name: Sourcegraph Amp
tools.standout: BYO-key at cost; 'orbs' (per-minute, auto-pause); outcome pricing per merged changeset; Agentic Batch Changes across hundreds-thousands of repos showing changeset mergeability (mergeable/conflicting/blocked).
tools.concurrency: Batch Changes across many repos (not one repo).
tools.pricing: Hobby free to $20 to Gigawatt; Teams $0; Enterprise custom; per-merged-changeset outcome pricing (outlier worth copying).

tools.name: OpenHands
tools.what: Open-source agent platform; closest prior art (verified NOT implementing the premise in the strong sense).
tools.standout: One-to-thousands agents; Large Codebase SDK claims multiple agents work in parallel 'without conflicts' via dependency-ordered sequencing; Agent Control Plane (governance); MIT core; Option 3 = per-conversation Docker sandboxes; docs tell the user to use worktrees/dirs to avoid conflicting edits.
tools.concurrency: Concurrent conversations each in its own sandbox; sub-agent delegation within a conversation.
tools.conflict: Isolation-based avoidance + static-analysis dependency sequencing (prevention, not merge/lock/detect).
tools.triage: None for reconciling parallel proposals; verified no visual triage UX.
tools.context: Agent Canvas + session state; MCP; ACP.
tools.pricing: Free OSS to $20 Pro (at-cost LLM) to Enterprise/self-hosted VPC; Individual caps 10 conversations/day.
tools.stack: Agent Canvas + CLI + Cloud; ACP; MCP.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.standout: Subagents with isolated contexts; parallel sessions; Agent Teams (<=15 subagents, claim); hooks/skills/subagents; Agent SDK; MCP.
tools.conflict: Isolated contexts; no shared-repo conflict engine.
tools.context: Agent SDK; hooks; skills; subagent memory.

tools.name: Superset
tools.what: Open-source agentic IDE running 100+ CLI agents in isolated worktrees.
tools.standout: Worktree-per-task; fleet dashboard; diff review; presets; PR feedback; orchestration APIs; 'Race Agents on One Task'; reliably 5-7 agents, goal 100; 'the real limit is how many independent, well-scoped tasks you can produce and review'; 14.8k downloads.
tools.conflict: Avoidance by worktree isolation; no shared-repo conflict engine.
tools.stack: git worktree isolation; any CLI agent.

tools.name: sigbound
tools.what: Closest shipping prior art to the premise (~80%); Go, Apache-2.0, ~50 stars, created 2026-07.
tools.standout: Parallel agents in worktrees then merges the work; model conflict resolution flags low-confidence cases for review; gates merge on build/test; self-repair; file lanes; repo-owned sigbound.policy; 'run parking' holds sensitive paths for human sig ack; sig serve HTTP API + UI for reviewing conflicts and acking parked landings; multi-machine bundles.
tools.concurrency: Parallel worktree agents with file lanes.
tools.conflict: Detects + model-resolves conflicts, parks low-confidence/sensitive edits behind human ack.
tools.triage: sig serve UI (conflict review + ack) + CLI.

tools.name: Cursor Origin
tools.what: Agent-native git forge embedded in Cursor (closed beta Aug 2026).
tools.standout: Cloud agents in isolated VMs; 'Origin' hosting + PR subscription (agent monitors CI and fixes checks); sigbound's own compare bills it as the closed hosted version of parallel + merge + AI conflict resolution + gated + self-repair.

tools.name: clash
tools.what: Read-only cross-worktree conflict detector; Rust, MIT, ~65 stars, 2026-02.
tools.standout: Detects conflicts across git worktrees using git merge-tree; fires as a Claude Code pre-write hook; conflict matrix TUI; watch mode; JSON output for orchestrators.

tools.name: weave (ataraxy-labs)
tools.what: Entity-level Git merge driver; MIT; npm @ataraxy-labs/sem.
tools.standout: Replaces line-based 3-way merge; auto-resolves false conflicts when two agents edit the same file differently; surfaces real contextual conflicts.

tools.name: CAID (arXiv 2603.21489, Jul 2026)
tools.standout: Branch-and-merge coordination built on git worktree/commit/merge primitives; per-agent self-verification + self conflict resolution at commit time; benchmarks Commit0/PaperBench; closest architectural match to the premise.
tools.conflict: Self conflict resolution at commit time.

tools.name: grite (arXiv 2606.19616, Jun 2026)
tools.what: Research: server-less git-native multi-agent coordination substrate.
tools.standout: Signed append-only coordination log stored in git; advisory leases + shared task state reduce duplicate/conflicting work; pre-PR coordination dataset.

tools.name: CodeCRDT (arXiv 2510.18893, Oct 2025)
tools.what: Research: CRDT-coordinated multi-agent LLM coding (600-trial study).
tools.standout: 100% convergence, zero merge failures; up to 21.1% speedup on some tasks and up to 39.4% slowdown on others; residual semantic conflict rate 5-10%; key finding: CRDTs solve transport, never correctness.
tools.concurrency: Lock-free concurrent code generation with strong eventual consistency.
tools.conflict: Character-level CRDT convergence; 5-10% semantic conflicts remain.
tools.triage: None (evidence that human review + decision log are load-bearing).

tools.name: GitHub (Agent HQ)
tools.standout: Agent HQ unites agents from Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/Cognition/xAI; mission control; agent identity; one-click merge conflict resolution; agentic code review; Code Quality; control plane; metrics; third-party agents are GitHub Apps; MCP Registry; native merge queue + gh stack; 180M developers; 'LGTM doesn't always mean the code is healthy'.
tools.concurrency: Multiple concurrent agent sessions; conflict avoidance pushed to humans ('be thoughtful about partitioning work').
tools.conflict: One-click merge conflict resolution; no cross-agent conflict engine.
tools.triage: PR review + mission control (watch/steer logs, batching).
tools.pricing: Free to Copilot Pro $10 to Pro+ $39 to Max to Business/Enterprise (usage-based from 2026-06).

tools.name: GitLab (Duo Agent Platform)
tools.standout: Agentic Chat; Planner/Security/Data Analyst agents; custom agents (AI Catalog); external agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI); flows incl issue-to-MR, code review, Fix CI/CD, SAST; autonomous merge-conflict resolution; governance dashboard; MCP tools; names the 'AI paradox' (only ~20% of dev time is writing code).
tools.conflict: Native autonomous merge-conflict resolution ('resolve merge conflicts, edit conflicting files, push a resolution commit') - strongest shipped competitor feature.
tools.pricing: Free to Premium $29/user to Ultimate; Duo Pro $19/user; Credits $12/$24 per user/mo.

tools.name: Bitbucket (Rovo Dev)
tools.standout: Rovo Dev is context-aware (planning/coding/reviews); AI code review; agentic CI/CD; Teamwork Graph couples Jira/Confluence context; Rovo CLI with Claude/Codex.
tools.pricing: Free <=5 to Standard $3.65/user to Premium; Rovo Dev $20/dev/mo (2,000 credits).

tools.name: Forgejo
tools.standout: ForgeFed/ActivityPub federation; Forgejo Actions; v15 JWT federated Actions identities; Pagure migration; MIT-adjacent OSS.

tools.name: Codeberg
tools.standout: Members voted 358-144 (14 abstentions) to restrict 'vibe-coded' projects and reject LLM training on hosted data; crawler defenses; hosts Gentoo mirror.
tools.context: AI opt-out must be first-class; hosted-data training refusal.

tools.name: Tangled
tools.standout: knots (headless Git hosts), spindles (MicroVM CI), appview; stacked PRs; seven XRPC webhook methods; identity = ATProto; 7,000+ users; EUR 3.8M seed.

tools.name: Radicle
tools.standout: Sovereign P2P, no central entity; Heartwood (3rd-gen); delegate-based canonical branch; disclosed two critical wire-protocol vulns (cleartext private repos, node impersonation) requiring a breaking migration to Iroh (QUIC/TLS).

tools.name: Cloudflare Workers
tools.standout: CPU-time is the binding constraint (10ms free / 5min paid, default 30s); HTTP wall time unlimited while connected; 128MB/isolate; 6 concurrent waiting-for-headers; up to 10,000 (configurable 10M) subrequests.
tools.pricing: Free to $5/mo + $0.30/M req, $0.02/M CPU-ms (10M req + 30M CPU-ms included).

tools.name: Cloudflare Durable Objects
tools.what: Stateful single-writer coordination actor with embedded SQLite.
tools.standout: One globally-unique, single-threaded object per key; embedded SQLite (10GB/object, value <=2MB, WS msg <=32MiB); hibernation 'allows the object to hibernate without disconnecting clients when idle' so review rooms are cheap when idle; ~1,000 req/s soft cap; unlimited objects per namespace; recommended shape one DO per repo/room (100 DOs x 100 hibernatable WS ~ $20.65/mo vs ~$142.95/mo non-hibernating).
tools.concurrency: One DO per repo/room as coordination hub; scale is horizontal.
tools.conflict: Single-writer serialization per object; natural place for leases/locks.
tools.triage: Realtime review rooms via hibernatable WebSockets.
tools.context: SQLite state per object; change-set index, agent roster, finding ledger.
tools.pricing: Free to $0.15/M req, $12.50/M GB-s (1M req + 400k GB-s included).
tools.stack: DO + SQLite; alarms; WebSocket Hibernation API.

tools.name: Cloudflare Workflows
tools.standout: 50,000 concurrent instances; 300 instances/s created; 2M queued; <=25,000 steps; step.sleep <=365 days; 1GB state/instance; waiting instances do not consume concurrency slots (millions may sleep); v2 control plane (SousChef + Gatekeeper).
tools.concurrency: 50k concurrent; millions sleeping free of slots.
tools.conflict: Per-step retries; waitForEvent human approval gates.

tools.name: Cloudflare Containers + Sandbox SDK
tools.standout: Each instance is a microVM with its own kernel and network; lite (1/16 vCPU, 256MiB) to standard-4 (4 vCPU, 12GiB); account limits 6 TiB memory / 1,500 vCPU / 30 TB disk; Sandbox SDK adds PTY, R2 mounts, agent-CLI runners; GA at Agents Week.
tools.concurrency: 1,500 concurrent vCPU per account is the hard ceiling on simultaneous heavy sandboxes.

tools.name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
tools.what: Agent runtime/harness: agent = Durable Object + SQLite + fibers.
tools.standout: Each agent runs on a DO with its own SQL, WebSocket connections and scheduling; scales to tens of millions of instances; runFiber() persists work in SQLite so it can be recovered; startFiber() gives durable acceptance/safe dedupe retries; onFiberRecovered(); sub-agents share the parent alarm slot.
tools.concurrency: Isolated per-agent DO; tens of millions of instances.
tools.conflict: Single-writer per agent DO; sessions/routing built in.

tools.name: Cloudflare Artifacts
tools.what: Git-compatible repo storage for tens of millions of repos.
tools.standout: Create tens of millions of repos, fork from any remote, hand off a URL to any Git client; pushes publish cf.artifacts.repo.pushed; Workers binding can fork the project for an agent, read files, and issue repo-scoped Git tokens; US/EU jurisdiction per namespace; the competition explicitly asks for 'the layer above it: how agents coordinate their work, how changes are reviewed and merged'.
tools.conflict: None by itself; the coordination layer is what must be built.

tools.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
tools.standout: Caching, rate-limit, retries, fallback, BYOK, analytics, ZDR; 10 gateways free / 20 paid; 1-line SDK; routing across providers.
tools.concurrency: Rate-limit/fallback across a fleet of agents.

tools.name: Cloudflare internal AI code reviewer (case study)
tools.what: Cloudflare's own CI-native multi-agent reviewer - the reference template.
tools.standout: 131,246 review runs across 48,095 MRs in 5,169 repos; median 3m39s; mean cost $1.19 (median $0.98, P99 $4.45); tiers trivial $0.20 / lite $0.67 / full $1.68; 85.7% cache hits; up to seven specialists; 'break glass' only 0.6%; findings persisted across re-reviews via MCP; honest limits (architecture awareness, cross-system impact, concurrency bugs, cost scaling with diff size).
tools.concurrency: Coordinator + specialist sub-reviewers with risk-tiered fan-out.
tools.triage: Prepared briefing over one shared cached context file; risk-tiered review depth.
tools.context: One shared cached context file; MCP-persisted findings ledger.
tools.stack: Coordinator + specialists on the Cloudflare stack.

tools.name: Repomix
tools.standout: Whole-repo to a single AI-friendly file (plain/XML/Markdown); token counting; split output; gitignore-aware; MCP; 28,502 stars; MIT.

tools.name: AGENTS.md
tools.standout: Repo-root instructions; nested 'closest file wins' for monorepos; ~20,000+ repos; formalized Aug 2025 by OpenAI/Google/Cursor/Factory/Sourcegraph; Linux Foundation-governed; static file with no runtime sync.
tools.context: Static intent layer (a file, not live coordination).

tools.name: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
tools.standout: Donated to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Dec 2025, co-founded by Anthropic/Block/OpenAI with support from Google/Microsoft/AWS/Cloudflare/Bloomberg; >10,000 servers (18,000+ indexed by 2026); spec mandates OAuth 2.1 resource-server model and forbids token passthrough; 'MUST NOT use sessions for authentication'.
tools.context: Context transport (MCP resources for live state); Cloudflare is a founding AAIF supporter.

tools.name: Spec Kit
tools.standout: spec -> plan -> tasks; works with 20+ agents; 104,718 stars; MIT; Thoughtworks Radar 'Assess'; maturity ladder spec-first to spec-anchored to spec-as-source; no shared spec format across tools.
tools.context: Spec artifacts as source of truth (snapshot, not live).

tools.name: Git AI
tools.what: Line-level AI provenance in Git Notes.
tools.standout: On commit, stores line-level attribution data in Git Notes linking each line of AI-generated code to agent/model/session; survives rebases, merges, stash/pops, squashes, resets, cherry-picks; publishes attribution standard v3.0.0; now part of OpenAI.
tools.context: Per-line, rebase-safe authorship provenance keyed to agent/model/session.
tools.stack: Git extension; Git Notes; spec v3.0.0.

tools.name: DeepWiki
tools.standout: Indexes repos and produces wikis with architecture diagrams and source links; exposes a remote no-auth MCP server with 3 tools (a compact, stealable interface).
tools.context: Code intelligence packaged as MCP tools.

tools.name: ast-grep / Semgrep
tools.what: Structural AST search and static analysis.
tools.standout: ast-grep searches/rewrites by AST pattern via tree-sitter (15.8k stars, MIT); Semgrep does semantic patterns over 30+ languages (16,816 stars); both structural, neither merges.

tools.name: OpenRewrite / Moderne
tools.standout: OpenRewrite recipes run one repo at a time; Moderne pre-computes LSTs across every repo then runs recipes in parallel, opening coordinated pull requests with a full audit trail.

tools.name: Difftastic
tools.standout: Syntax-aware diff; maintainer states 'AST merging is a hard problem that difftastic does not address' - clear evidence that structural merge is unsolved whitespace.

tools.name: Unblocked
tools.standout: Reconciles conflicts between code/chat/docs/prod sources; enforces existing access controls; delivers ranked, compressed context to any MCP client; ingestion rebuilt on Temporal durable execution; SOC2; $19-$29/user/mo.
tools.context: Rank + compress + ACL-gate context; durable ingestion.

tools.name: Whiteboard (dev.fast)
tools.what: Direct prior art for visual/spatial agent-drawn review; YC W26, MIT, 1.7k stars.
tools.standout: A canvas the existing agent draws on through an MCP server, so a large agent-written change arrives as a structured 'whiteboard session' instead of a 40-file diff; diagrams linked to code (pinned line ranges); Rust AST-aware semantic diff; decision log ('records which decisions were your requirements and which the agent made alone'); writes use an authoring lease per review so two agents cannot silently overwrite each other; every saved version keeps command inputs as receipts. Limits: single-repo, ~736MB build, snapshot-only sharing, no editing.
tools.concurrency: Authoring lease per review (advisory lock per review).
tools.conflict: Authoring lease + per-version command receipts prevent concurrent-writer clobbering.
tools.triage: Canvas review; decision log; command receipts.

tools.name: CodeSee
tools.standout: Review Maps create diagrams from pull requests; automatic multi-language maps.

tools.name: AppMap
tools.standout: Provides runtime evidence for AI-assisted development: calls, queries, exceptions, side effects (execution traces, not just static maps).

tools.name: Mermaid / D2 / ZenUML
tools.standout: Text diagrams dominate docs; ZenUML is JS-based, needs no server, ships a visual modeling plugin for Codex and Claude Code; Mermaid renders ZenUML sequence diagrams; diagrams are static and not resolvable to code (the gap Whiteboard attacks).
tools.context: Diagrams not linked to code line ranges.

tools.name: Yjs
tools.standout: Network agnostic (p2p); scales to an unlimited number of users; rich adapter ecosystem; de-facto text standard; MIT.
tools.conflict: Character-level CRDT convergence; no semantic merge.

tools.name: Automerge 3
tools.standout: JSON-tree generalist; Automerge 3 cut document size roughly 10x via column-oriented storage; strong TypeScript story; better fit than Yjs for a canvas of code nodes/threads.
tools.conflict: CRDT convergence on tree/map; no semantic code merge.

tools.name: Loro
tools.standout: Movable Tree as a first-class primitive; where concurrent moves on Yjs can produce cycles or orphaned nodes, Loro guarantees it at the algorithm level; Fugue text; time travel; ~970KB WASM gzipped; thin adapter ecosystem, no canonical server.

tools.name: Liveblocks
tools.standout: Presence/comments/notifications/AI copilots (AI editors that join the room like collaborators); meters collaboration minutes, comments, storage, notifications; MAU Unlimited on all plans per current docs (Free real caps: 500 active rooms, 10 simultaneous connections/room, 3,000 collaboration minutes, 200 comments).
tools.pricing: Free (capped) to metered tiers; multi-region + self-host Enterprise only.

tools.name: PartyKit
tools.what: Sync SaaS - already owned by Cloudflare.
tools.standout: Cloudflare acquired PartyKit (Apr 2024); deploys to your own Cloudflare account on workerd/Durable Objects; Yjs via y-partykit; 'deploy to your own Cloudflare account and pay for the resources you use'.
tools.concurrency: DO-room based realtime (one room per object).
tools.conflict: Yjs/CRDT backed; DO single-writer per room.
tools.pricing: Free to Workers usage ($0.30/1M req; $0.50/M GB-s).

tools.name: Jazz
tools.standout: Local-first relational database with row-level permissions and real-time sync; no separate API layer; uses the same Rust database engine core everywhere (client and server).

tools.name: ElectricSQL
tools.standout: Syncs Postgres to SQLite in a 'Shape' - a SQL where clause selects a partial dataset; written in Elixir; logical replication.
tools.context: Predicate-based partial sync (shape) for per-agent scoping.

tools.name: tldraw
tools.standout: 50.7k stars; license adapted from the Scratch license - must preserve 'Made with tldraw' watermark unless a business license is purchased; multiplayer sync included; canvas-specific realtime sync (tldraw sync).
tools.pricing: Free with watermark to paid business license.

tools.name: React Flow (xyflow)
tools.standout: Node-graph SDK; MIT core plus a separate perpetual, non-transferable Pro license; the default for diagram/flow editors.

tools.name: PixiJS
tools.standout: WebGL and WebGPU renderers; fastest, most lightweight 2D library; MIT.

tools.name: Temporal
tools.standout: Workflows and activities: sequential code whose history replays on crash; you run workers that poll; polyglot; 99.99% HA; billed per action.
tools.pricing: $50 per million actions (to $25/M), $0.042/GBhr active storage; $150 credits entry.

tools.name: Restate
tools.standout: Journals durable handlers and virtual objects (stateful entities keyed by ID) inside a compact single-binary runtime; orchestration managed, handlers on your infra; the virtual-object idea maps directly onto one Durable Object per agent session.
tools.concurrency: Single-writer ID-keyed virtual objects (maps to one DO per session).

tools.name: E2B
tools.standout: Firecracker per sandbox with its own kernel; ~150ms start; fork; Apache-2.0; Hobby 20 concurrent, Pro 100 expandable to 1,100, Enterprise tens of thousands.
tools.pricing: $100 credit to $150/mo + $0.0504/vCPU-h + $0.0162/GiB-h (billed per second, wall-clock - idle time bills).

tools.name: Modal
tools.standout: gVisor isolation; GPU sandboxes; documents operation at 100,000+ concurrent sandboxes (up to 50,000 concurrent per customer); meters provisioned resources while running and nothing while idle (active-CPU billing, unlike E2B/Daytona wall-clock).
tools.conflict: gVisor userspace kernel (10-30% syscall overhead on I/O-heavy work).
tools.pricing: $30 credit; ~3x function rate; per-second, active-CPU billing.

tools.name: Daytona
tools.standout: Sub-90ms start; container default with Kata/gVisor opt-in; vCPU pools 10 to 500 by tier; same unit price as E2B ($0.0504/vCPU-h + $0.0162/GiB-h) but wall-clock metering.

tools.name: Fly Machines
tools.standout: Firecracker microVMs; suspend/resume keeps memory; 100-500ms wake; per-second billing by CPU/RAM.

tools.name: Firecracker
tools.standout: Rust microVMs; boot in ~100-200ms; KVM for hardware-enforced isolation; the defensible default for adversarial multi-tenant agent code (dedicated kernel per sandbox).

tools.name: gVisor
tools.standout: Userspace kernel written in Go; no nested virtualization; used by Modal and Beam; adds 10-30% syscall-interception overhead on I/O-heavy workloads; shares the host kernel (weaker than Firecracker for adversarial code).

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK
tools.standout: Claude-driven loop with built-in file, shell, MCP, hook, permission and subagent capabilities; the 2026 direction is harnesses (loop + context + permissions + persistence + subagents) replacing bare frameworks; closest harness shape to a git platform.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.standout: Explicit nodes, edges, state transitions and checkpoints; HITL interrupts; graph-routing coordination pattern; OSS plus a paid platform.

tools.name: gitleaks
tools.category: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain
tools.standout: Most trusted open-source secret scanner (16M->20M docker downloads, 17k->19k stars, MIT); regex+entropy; top recall (88%); GitHub Action; gitleaks.toml rules.

tools.name: TruffleHog
tools.category: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain
tools.standout: Classifies over 800 secret types and can log in to confirm whether a secret is live or not; verification is its edge.

tools.name: SOPS + git-crypt (secret-typed files)
tools.category: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain
tools.standout: Mechanism proven: git-crypt transparently encrypts chosen files at commit when paths/attributes match and decrypts on checkout, enabling secret material in the same repo without locking the whole repo; git-sops keeps the worktree decrypted while the git index, blobs and remote stay encrypted; SOPS stores keys in cleartext and encrypts only values. No agent-aware policy layer exists.
tools.context: Secret-typed files (ciphertext in repo; plaintext never in a blob with git-sops).

tools.name: SPIFFE / SPIRE
tools.category: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain
tools.standout: spiffe:// SVIDs (X.509 + JWT); a single OAuth client identifier can represent an agent platform running many concurrent agent instances (IETF draft-mcguinness); companion drafts say agents should use SPIFFE, WIMSE, OAuth and OpenID SSF; the model IETF builds on.
tools.concurrency: One identity per concurrent agent instance (IETF instance profile).
tools.conflict: Cryptographic per-instance identity enables independent scopes/revocation.

tools.name: Okta/Auth0 for AI Agents
tools.category: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain
tools.standout: Auth for MCP; Agent as Principal; On-Behalf-Of; Token Vault; 'Auth0 now secures MCP and autonomous agents as first-class identities'; OAuth token exchange; Microsoft frames MCP/A2A/OAuth/SPIFFE as the backbone; identity is becoming commodity, differentiation shifts to policy over identity.

tools.name: SLSA
tools.category: Trust Layer: Secrets, Identity & Supply Chain
tools.standout: Levels 1-4 with in-toto attestations; 'provenance doesn't do anything unless somebody inspects it. SLSA calls that inspection verification'; sigstore/Fulcio/Rekor underpin keyless signing in the SLSA GitHub generator.

tools.name: GitClear
tools.standout: 623M changes analysed: cross-file function calls down 35%, refactoring line moves down 70%, long-term legacy maintenance down 74% vs 2022; copy/paste +41%, code-block duplication +81%, error-masking +47%, two-week churn +15%; Diff Delta per-model attribution; live industry charts.

tools.name: DX
tools.standout: 4-dimension AI framework (speed, effectiveness, quality, impact); TrueThroughput; PR Cycle Time; PR Revert Rate; Developer Experience Index (DXI); 'AI output explains 63% of developer time savings but shows a weak link to increased innovation ratio'.

tools.name: LinearB
tools.standout: DORA + leading indicators; AI-aware automation; benchmarks from 8.1M+ pull requests across 4,800+ organizations.
